target_customer: Traditional proximity retailers (small grocery shops) in Morocco, Tunisia and francophone Africa
problem: Small shops buy stock through fragmented wholesalers with cash and little credit; they lack digital ordering and financial services.
business_model: B2B ordering and delivery margin, then fintech (credit, payments, BaaS)

founders.name: Ismael Belkhayat
education: Studied in Paris, London, Madrid and Ithaca (Cornell)

competitors.name: TradeDepot
competitors.what: Nigerian B2B retail ordering and credit for small shops

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering app plus logistics; the hard parts are operations, credit risk and later regulated payments.

defensibility.rationale: Reach over half of Casablanca proximity stores by Oct 2021, Karny.ma bookkeeping base and a 2025 payment-institution licence from Bank Al-Maghrib.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy or buyout found through 2026; Chari acquired Karny.ma (2021) and Diago (Cote d'Ivoire, 2022).

market_need_then: Casablanca alone had about 20,000 proximity stores; Chari reached 10,000 within a year of launch and offered free delivery under 24 hours.

branding.domain_note: Early site was chari.ma; now chari.com.
branding.community_and_virality: Forbes Middle East listed Sophia Alj among 20 women behind tech brands (2022); coverage as the first Moroccan YC startup (July 2021).

brand_strength.rationale: Strong local press presence and market share in Casablanca; no source examines the name or visual identity.

pivots.to: Merchant super app and banking-as-a-service with payment institution licence
pivots.why: Fintech and licensed payments for merchants; BNPL piloted since Jan 2022

outcome_analysis: Chari grew fast in Casablanca, raised a $5M seed at a reported $70M valuation within four weeks of Demo Day, a bridge at $100M in January 2022, and a $12M Series A in October 2025 with a Bank Al-Maghrib payment licence. The long gap between rounds and shift toward fintech suggest unit economics in grocery distribution needed financial services. It remains active with about $17M raised.
notes: Founder surname of Sophia is given as Alj in most sources and Belkhayat in one. Wamda states $17M total raised including the Series A. Bridge amount undisclosed. The only dated competitor source is TechCrunch Jan 2022 (six months after S21) and lists similar African B2B retail firms (also Payflex, LipaLater, Carbon Zero); none was confirmed to operate in Morocco in 2021. Aggregator-listed $1M Endeavor Catalyst Series A investment unverified. Name origin not found in any source seen.
